problemStatement.formal: \text{For any finite set of } \geq 3 \text{ points in } \mathbb{R}^2 \text{, not all collinear, there exists a line through exactly 2 of them.}
problemStatement.plain: The Sylvester-Gallai theorem: given any finite set of ≥3 points in the plane, not all on a line, there exists a line through exactly 2 of them (an 'ordinary line').
whyMatters: Kelly's 1948 extremal proof is elegant and formalizable
Foundational for combinatorial geometry results including Green-Tao's ordinary lines theorem
